name: Compute Hardware
oneLiner: The chips that do the maths: GPUs and other accelerators, their fast memory, and the links between them.

analogy.text: A kitchen: chips are the cooks, memory is the counter space, and interconnect is how fast cooks can pass dishes to each other.
analogy.breaks: Cooks work independently. Thousands of accelerators must act as one machine in lockstep, so the network between them matters as much as the chips.

givesAbove: Raw arithmetic throughput and memory, exposed to software through platforms such as CUDA or ROCm.
needsBelow: Power, cooling and fabricated silicon from Physical & Energy.
